claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi is a multicomponent, quinary high-entropy alloy system.
Equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi is an example of the intended alloy compositions.
The intended initial state is a multicomponent HEA liquid at or near its high melting temperature.
Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM reference with an MLIP trained specifically on ab initio HEA-liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Adaptive sampling and uncertainty quantification can be used to develop the proposed MLIP from ab initio liquid configurations.
The proposed method applies over approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
Multicomponent HEA liquids in this temperature range exhibit vast configurational diversity.
A liquid-trained MLIP will capture more of the local atomic configurations in the liquid than the EAM reference.
Capturing more local configurations will diminish the discrepancy between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Training on a large and diverse ab initio liquid dataset enables the MLIP to represent rare and complex liquid configurations.
On-the-fly uncertainty quantification allows the potential-energy-surface model to adapt to insufficiently sampled configurations.
Closer tracking of the ab initio target potential by the MLIP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The MLIP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The MLIP-based calculation will achieve a free-energy deviation below approximately 5 meV/atom relative to fully converged ab initio calculations.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately represent the full configurational landscape of ab initio multicomponent HEA liquids.
The advantage of the MLIP may be diminished for simpler alloys or at lower temperatures because their configurational diversity is less pronounced.
Existing elemental and binary calculations support the viability of MLIPs for capturing complex atomic environments.
The quantitative result depends on the quality of the ab initio training data and the effectiveness of adaptive sampling.
